title: Conditional Access and Azure role-based access control
learningObjective: Describe how Microsoft Entra Conditional Access uses signals to make access decisions, and how Azure RBAC grants permissions at a scope.
foundation: Conditional Access is an if-then engine for sign-ins: IF a user signs in from an unknown country, THEN require MFA (or block). It looks at who, where, what device and which app.

Azure role-based access control (RBAC) decides what a signed-in person can do with Azure resources. You assign a role (for example Reader) to a person or group at a scope (for example a resource group).
Authentication is 'who are you?' (Entra ID, MFA, Conditional Access). Authorization is 'what may you do?' (RBAC).
engineer: Conditional Access signals: user or group membership, location (IP ranges, countries), device (platform, compliant or hybrid-joined), application, sign-in and user risk (with Microsoft Entra ID P2). Decisions: block access; grant access; grant with requirements (MFA, compliant device, approved app, password change, terms of use). Requires Microsoft Entra ID P1.

Common policies: require MFA for administrators; require MFA from outside trusted locations; block legacy authentication; require compliant devices for sensitive apps; block sign-ins from certain countries.

RBAC elements: security principal (user, group, service principal, managed identity) + role definition (set of permissions) + scope (management group, subscription, resource group, resource) = role assignment.

Built-in roles: Owner (full access including access management), Contributor (full resource management, no access management), Reader (view only), User Access Administrator (manage access only), plus 100s of service-specific roles (for example Virtual Machine Contributor). You can create custom roles.

RBAC is additive and inherited down the hierarchy; it's enforced on any action through Azure Resource Manager (portal, CLI, PowerShell, templates). Follow least privilege: smallest role, narrowest scope, groups instead of individuals.

example.title: A finance team
body: Policy: IF a finance app is opened from outside the office, THEN require MFA and a compliant device. Sign-ins from countries where the company doesn't operate are blocked.
In Azure, the finance-ops group has Contributor on rg-finance only; auditors have Reader on the subscription; nobody gets Owner except two admins.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Owner or User Access Administrator to assign Azure roles; Conditional Access Administrator for policies
limits: Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher
portal: Microsoft Entra admin center > Protection > Conditional Access > New policy (users, target resources, conditions, grant).
Resource / resource group / subscription > Access control (IAM) > Add role assignment.
configuration.cli:
az role assignment create --assignee <user-or-group-id> --role Reader --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/rg-finance
az role definition list --query "[?roleType=='BuiltInRole'].roleName" -o tsv | head

lab.objective: See authentication, Conditional Access and RBAC decisions.
steps: Sign-in and access tab: run the default, then each preset; change role and action.
Built-in Azure roles tab: answer every requirement.
expected: MFA satisfies the Conditional Access policy
RBAC decides the action after sign-in
failureScenarios: Giving Owner when Contributor is enough
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: User signed in but gets 'authorization failed'.
troubleshooting.cause: No role assignment at that scope.
troubleshooting.fix: Assign the needed role at the right scope.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users outside the office can't sign in at all.
troubleshooting.cause: A policy blocks instead of requiring MFA.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the grant control to 'Require MFA'.

comparisons.difference: Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions; RBAC controls actions on Azure resources.
Azure roles manage Azure resources; Microsoft Entra roles (such as User Administrator) manage the directory.

misconceptions.myth: Contributor can grant access to others.
misconceptions.reality: Only Owner or User Access Administrator.

misconceptions.myth: Conditional Access is included in every Entra ID edition.
Deny is the default role effect.
misconceptions.reality: RBAC is additive; no assignment means no access.

architectureDecisions: Assign roles to groups at the narrowest scope.
Require MFA for all admins with Conditional Access.
